subject: Chemistry
description: Common element uses, chemical names of daily substances, symbols

questions.stem: The chemical name of BAKING SODA is:
questions.explanation: Baking soda = sodium hydrogen carbonate (sodium bicarbonate). Washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. Caustic soda = NaOH. Common salt = NaCl.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which METAL is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal liquid at ordinary room temperature (melting point −39 °C). Gallium melts in the hand (~30 °C) but is solid at typical room temperature of 20-25 °C. Bromine is the only liquid non-metal at room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Match the CHEMICAL NAME with its COMMON NAME. A. Calcium hydroxide.  B. Calcium carbonate.  C. Sodium chloride.  D. Potassium nitrate. List-II: 1. Slaked lime.  2. Limestone / marble.  3. Common salt.  4. Saltpetre.
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)₂ — slaked lime (used in whitewashing). CaCO₃ — limestone/marble/chalk. NaCl — common salt. KNO₃ — saltpetre (used in gunpowder).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The element that makes up nearly 65% of the human body by MASS is:
questions.explanation: By mass: Oxygen ~65% (mostly in water and organic molecules), Carbon ~18%, Hydrogen ~10%, Nitrogen ~3%. By ATOM count however, Hydrogen is most abundant. This trap is common in NTPC papers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which gas is produced when SODIUM is added to water?
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂↑. The reaction is exothermic; ignites the H₂ gas (yellow-orange flame, since Na imparts yellow colour). Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al ... (only those above hydrogen displace H from water).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The PUREST form of NATURAL IRON is:
questions.explanation: Wrought iron: ~99.5% pure iron, <0.25% carbon — malleable. Pig iron: from blast furnace, ~4% carbon — brittle. Cast iron: remelted pig iron with controls, 2-4% carbon. Steel: alloy of iron + carbon 0.2-2% + other elements — most commercially used.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The chemical symbol for GOLD is:
questions.explanation: Au (from Latin 'aurum'). Silver = Ag (argentum). Iron = Fe (ferrum). Sodium = Na (natrium). Potassium = K (kalium). Tungsten = W (wolfram). Latin origins trip many candidates.
